update_notes: 2026-01-03: MCO-010にRMAT指定・EMA Orphan指定追加、jCells NCT追加、SPVN06 PRODYGY試験詳細追加、ZM-02 PRISM試験NCT追加、VG901試験完了予定更新

recent_updates.event: BLA rolling submission in progress (started July 2025). Full submission expected early 2026 with priority review eligibility. ICER (April 2025) concluded evidence demonstrates net health benefit. EMA granted Orphan designations for 5 categories of retinal dystrophies. RMAT designation for Stargardt disease
5-year safety data and 3-year efficacy data show sustained vision gains. BLA expected to be completed in early 2026 with priority review eligibility
REMAIN study: Durable 3-year vision improvements with favorable safety profile
Initiated rolling BLA submission to FDA
RESTORE trial met primary endpoint with statistical significance

MCO-010.notes: First gene-agnostic gene therapy for RP (sonpiretigene isteparvovec). Uses AAV2 vector to deliver multi-characteristic opsin (MCO) to bipolar retinal cells via intravitreal injection. Full BLA submission expected early 2026, eligible for priority review. One-time in-office injection for severe vision loss. ICER (April 2025) concluded evidence adequately demonstrates net health benefit. Also pursuing Stargardt disease indication.

recent_updates.event: Phase 3 liMeliGhT trial enrollment nearing completion (US 15 sites ~150 patients: 75 RHO + 75 gene-agnostic, Canada up to 50 patients). Rolling BLA submission expected to start H1 2026. Top-line data expected Q4 2026. Primary endpoint completion Dec 31, 2026. EMA MAA eligible for centralized review
Phase 3 liMeliGhT trial (NCT06388200) enrollment nearing completion. Top-line data expected Q4 2026, commercialization projected for 2027
Phase 3 liMeliGhT trial actively enrolling (ClinicalTrials.gov updated)
FDA approved Expanded Access Program for up to 75 eligible patients in the US
Health Canada approved trial expansion to Canada (up to 50 subjects)
Phase 1/2 2-year data: 100% (9/9) patients improved or maintained vision
First patient dosed in Phase 3 liMeliGhT trial

OCU400.notes: Targets 100+ gene mutations. Expanded Access Program in US (75 patients) and Canada expansion (50 patients) approved.

recent_updates.event: Positive FDA meeting to finalize Phase 2/3 registrational study design
Positive Phase 1/2 results presented at ARVO: LLVA improvements, microperimetry improvements in 18 patients (PLATYPUS 12, WALLABY 6)
Phase 2/3 registrational trial planned for late 2025 following FDA guidance
Received FDA Rare Pediatric Disease (RPD) designation

VP-001.notes: First therapy specifically for RP11. Positive Phase 1/2 results with vision improvements reported by patients. RPD designation makes it eligible for Priority Review Voucher (PRV) worth $100M+ if approved.

recent_updates.event: Phase 2/3 VISTA trial actively enrolling globally. Additional regulatory designations: FDA Fast Track, UK ILAP, EU PRIME. Positive interim results from Phase 2 DAWN trial (May 2025)
Phase 2/3 VISTA trial enrollment completed. 12-month topline data expected in H2 2026
Received FDA RMAT designation. Phase 2 SKYLINE trial 12-month data: 63% responder rate
Phase 2 DAWN trial: 6-month interim data positive
Phase 2 DAWN trial: second eye treatment showed mean 16-letter improvement. $170M Series B funding completed
Received FDA RMAT designation
Phase 2/3 VISTA trial initiated

AGTC-501.notes: Targets X-linked RP. VISTA trial actively enrolling globally. Multiple positive Phase 2 trials. RMAT designation received Jan 2025, along with Fast Track, UK ILAP, and EU PRIME designations.

recent_updates.event: FDA Fast Track Designation granted Feb 27, 2025. First patient dosed July 8, 2025 in Phase 1/2a CLARICO trial (NCT06789445). Trial aims to enroll 54 participants to assess safety and outcomes
First patient treated in CLARICO trial - world's first iPSC-derived cell therapy tested in humans for primary photoreceptor diseases
Received FDA Fast Track designation

OpCT-001.notes: iPSC-derived photoreceptor cells. World's first iPSC-derived cell therapy for primary photoreceptor diseases. First patient dosed July 8, 2025. Aims to restore vision by replacing degenerated photoreceptor cells.

recent_updates.event: Received FDA Fast Track designation
First gene therapy trial for RP in Japan initiated
First patient dosed at Keio University Hospital

Keio_Optogenetics.notes: Targets completely blind RP patients. First RP gene therapy trial in Japan. Treatment designated as RV-001 by Restore Vision. Planning to enroll 6-15 severe patients with 6-month follow-up.

CTx-PDE6b.notes: Targets specific PDE6B mutations causing RP

recent_updates.event: PRODYGY Phase 1/2 trial progressing well. Dose escalation (Step 1) completed Oct 2024. Controlled, randomized extension phase (Step 2) started Q4 2024. Primary endpoint expected H2 2025 (12 months after last patient in Step 2). Favorable safety profile through 18 months: no SAEs, no DLTs, no discontinuations. Preliminary efficacy signals observed in Phase 1

SPVN06.notes: Gene-agnostic gene therapy for RP. PRODYGY trial evaluating safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy. Good safety profile demonstrated through 18 months with no serious adverse events. Primary endpoint expected H2 2025.

recent_updates.event: Phase 2b LUNA trial ongoing. 2-year study actively enrolling 81 participants (ages 8+). Trial sites in US, UK, and Netherlands. Latest update on ClinicalTrials.gov: October 2, 2025
First patient dosed in Phase 2b LUNA trial

Ultevursen.notes: Targets Usher syndrome type 2A and RP with USH2A mutations. 2-year trial with 81 participants ages 8 and up.

recent_updates.event: Phase 3 LUMEOS trial failed to meet primary endpoint

Botaretigene sparoparvovec.notes: Did not meet primary endpoint but showed improvements in secondary endpoints

recent_updates.event: Newly identified program

VG901.status: Active - Dose escalation in progress, trial expected to complete end of 2025

recent_updates.event: Phase 1b trial ongoing at University of Tübingen, Germany. Dose escalation proceeding after DSMB approval (Jan 2025). No dose-limiting toxicities in first dose cohort. Trial expected to complete by end of 2025. RPDD designation enables potential Priority Review Voucher upon approval
FDA granted Rare Pediatric Disease Designation (RPDD). DSMB unanimously approved dose escalation in ongoing Phase 1b trial
First patient dosed in Phase 1b trial

VG901.notes: Gene therapy for RP caused by CNGA1 mutations. Uses proprietary next-generation vgAAV capsid for intravitreal delivery of functional CNGA1 gene to photoreceptors. Trial conducted at University of Tübingen. RPDD makes it eligible for Priority Review Voucher if approved.

ZM-02.status: IND approved - PRISM trial active in US and China

recent_updates.event: PRISM trial (NCT07282457) is a multi-center, randomized, sham-controlled, dose-escalation Phase 1/2 study in US and China. MOON trial data presented at ATC (Nov 2025) showed significant improvements in vision, mobility, and color perception recovery. Gene-agnostic approach restores photosensitivity regardless of specific mutation
FDA approved IND application, enabling multinational Phase 1/2 PRISM trial in US and China
Received FDA Orphan Drug Designation

ZM-02.notes: Gene-agnostic optogenetic therapy. Bypasses degenerated photoreceptors to reactivate remaining inner retinal neural circuits. MOON trial in China showed promising initial clinical data with improvements in vision, mobility, and color perception.

jCells.status: Active - JC02-88 trial ongoing, first patient dosed Aug 2025

recent_updates.event: JC02-88 trial (NCT06912633) started June 20, 2025. First patient dosed Aug 18-20, 2025. Testing 8.8 million cells (~50% higher than previous highest dose) via single intravitreal injection. Randomized, blinded, sham-controlled design with up to 60 patients ages 18-60. 6-month trial with primary/full completion Sept 2026. Sham recipients eligible for treatment in extension study
Initiated new Phase 2 clinical trial (JC02-88) with higher dose of 8.8 million jCells
JC02-88 Phase 2 trial officially started

jCells.notes: Cell-based therapy (famzeletcel) for RP regardless of causative gene mutation. RMAT designation granted. Previous Phase 2b showed improvements in BCVA, contrast sensitivity, and visual field. New trial tests higher dose in sham-controlled design.
